forms.response_action: The contractor CMS working on an Area D fuel tank renovation were fueling equipment around the work area by moving the fuel tank around using a forklift. They lifted the secondary containment the fueling tank was sitting on, the secondary containment gave out under the weight of the tank and the tank tipped over spilling diesel fuel. The tank was picked back up onto the containment but the movement caused the tank to then tip backwards spilling more fuel. Overall 50 gallons of diesel was spilled, all of the fuel was contained to the Area D concrete dike system. The fuel was then surrounded with absorbents to keep the spill from spreading. The spill was cleaned up using buckets, absorbents and kitty litter. All of the used absorbents and kitty litter were collected into 55 gallon drums for disposal. The waste was manifested and picked up by Clean Harbors for disposal on 14 September 2026.

forms.waterway_affected: None directly; The flowpath of Rapid Creek almost encircles the site and ranges in distance from 420 feet to the west, 450 feet to the north, and 900 feet to the east
forms.cause_description: Likely associated with the operation of multiple UST systems from at least 1978 until 2025
forms.response_action: Three USTs (1 x 2k gal, 2 x 1k gal), product piping, and dispensers were removed; Approximately 7 tons of impacted soils were excavated from underneath the dispensers and transported to the Rapid City Landfill for proper disposal (October 13, 2025)
forms.comments: During removal activities, 13 soil samples were collected, screened with a PID, and subsequently submitted for laboratory analyses. Laboratory analytical results indicated measurable petroleum hydrocarbon concentrations in three soil samples collected from underneath the dispensers. Of these, two soil samples exceeded DANR Tier 1 Trigger Levels for Soils (2970 ppm TPH-D, 836 ppm TPH-G). Petroleum impacts appear localized beneath the dispensers. Groundwater was not encountered. Rapid Creek surrounds the site in all directions except south, ranging from 420 feet to the west, 450 feet to the north, and 900 feet to the west. [See AET Report No. P-0047712]

forms.response_action: On July 2, 2025 (Wednesday), approximately 9:00am, approximately 216 gallons of #2 diesel fuel were spilled within the concrete secondary containment associated with the above ground diesel fuel tanks that provide fuel to the Boiler Plant. The spill occurred due to an overflow of the #3 diesel fuel storage tank during filling. The fuel was contained within the secondary containment and an initial spill clean-up began immediately and concluded approximately 11am the same day. Four VA staff: 1) Transferred the spilled #2 diesel fuel into 5, 55-gallon drums, 2) Put down, in total, 5 bags of Oil-Dri (kitty litter) and 8 bags of oil absorbing PIG Mat Pulp as the liquid levels were receding via fuel removal, 3) After fuel removal, staff moved and shifted around the Oil-Dri and oil absorbing PIG Mat Pulp to increase the absorption of any remaining fuel, 4) Left the Oil-Dri and oil absorbing PIG Mat Pulp on the spilled area overnight because of, the amount of Oil-Dri and oil absorbing PIG Mat Pulp used during the initial spill clean-up; there was no rain forecasted for the rest of the day, overnight or the next day; and wanting to absorb as much of the diesel fuel as possible, 5) Cleaned/Wiped down all spill cleanup materials/equipment used with towels and oil absorbent mats and put them away. On July 3, 2025 (Thursday), from approximately 8:30am to approximately 9:30am, four VA staff: 1) Moved and shifted around the Oil-Dri and oil absorbing PIG Mat Pulp to increase the absorption of any remaining fuel while sweeping/picking up the Oil-Dri and oil absorbing PIG Mat Pulp, 2) Cleaned/Wiped down all spill cleanup materials/equipment used with towels and oil absorbent mats and put them away, 3) Put all fuel-contaminated materials, including PPE, into a 14-gallon drum, 4) Stored the 14-gallon and 55-gallon drums that will go out with our next off-site hazardous waste shipment. See pictures in the email which show the finished results after spill clean-up efforts.

records.title: Diesel Overfill Ellsworth Air force Base

forms.response_action: placed absorbents and pooled liquid pumped into drum

The contractor (CORRAY) working on Area D Fuel tank renovation was fueling a portable generator. During the fueling process they walked away from the generator and it overfilled, with excess fuel pouring out onto the pavement. When the contractor realized an estimated 100 gallons of fuel had been released. Each tank in the fuels area is surrounded by a secondary containment dike, so all fuel was contained on the pavement. Spill clean-up began immediately and was completed within the 24-hour cleanup window. The fuel was cleaned using absorbent pads and absorbent socks. The used absorbents were collected in 3 55-gallon drums (319 lbs) and taken to HAZMART to be properly disposed of. Because the fuel is non-hazardous the absorbents were wrung out in the HAZMART's centrifuge. The spun out fuel was collected for disposal as off-spec fuel, and the dry absorbents were disposed of in the garbage.

forms.location: 1940 EP Howe St, Bldg 8205 ELLSWORTH, SD 57706
forms.response_action: Once spill of hydraulic fluid was identified, petroleum absorbent booms were placed around the spill site. Aero Simulation coordinated efforts to evaluate environmental impact through American Engineering Testing (AET), and efforts to remove impacted soil and backfill area through Lee Earley, Inc. (LEi), both out of Rapid City, SD. AET took initial soil samples to evaluate extent of spill and coordinated final excavation efforts with LEi. LEi completed excavation of impacted soil, which was determined to be an area of approximately 9ft x 18ft and 1.5ft deep, on April 9, 2025. With soil removed from impacted area, AET took further samples and submitted for analysis to ensure no further presence of hydraulic fluid. LEi backfilled excavated area with similar soil type. AET received lab results back noting results did not indicate any detections of petroleum in the soil samples. AET provided a Report of Remedial Excavation to be submitted with this form, with the opinion that no additional assessment or remediation associated with this petroleum release is warranted.
